subject: Pilot request: adjusted uptime band and scaled credit for QuantumLytics
messages:
From: Eliot Smith <eliot.smith@quantumlytics.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot - uptime target discussion

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward with a three-week pilot. Before we start, Legal and Ops flagged one item: our regulatory environment requires a guaranteed minimum uptime band for inference services used in our pipeline.

QuantumLytics is proposing a pilot SLA that sets a 99.5% uptime target during business hours (M-F, 8am-6pm PT) with a scaled service credit if availability dips below 99.75% during that window. The standard Redwood terms we saw in the draft are 99.9% blanket uptime, which is fine for hosted, but our compliance team needs a tailored band and a proportional credit schedule for the pilot.

Can Redwood authorize a temporary adjusted uptime band for the pilot and a capped credit schedule? We want to move quickly but need that assurance in writing for our Procurement kickoff next week.

Attached: RL-SLA-draft-quantumlytics-v1.pdf

—Eliot
Eliot Smith
Director, Platform Ops | QuantumLytics
eliot.smith@quantumlytics.com
+1 415-555-0198
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Eliot Smith <eliot.smith@quantumlytics.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot - uptime target discussion

Hi Eliot — appreciate the clarity and the draft.

Short answer: we can consider a pilot-specific uptime band, but that requires Deal Desk + commercial approval because it changes remedy exposure. I'll start the conversation internally and share a concrete proposal by end of day Thursday.

Next steps for us:
- I'll run the impact analysis (estimated credit exposure) and attach a recommended scaled credit table.
- Loop Deal Desk and commercial (Avery) for pricing/terms.
- If needed, bring in Marissa for final signoff on non-standard remedies.

Could you confirm the pilot expected volume (avg tokens / minute) and whether you expect multi-region failover? That will affect the risk profile.

Attaching: pilot-metrics-forecast.xlsx (please confirm numbers)

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.com
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot - uptime target discussion

Forwarding Aisha's note — this is Deal Desk territory.

Quick read: customer requests pilot uptime band of 99.5% business hours with a scaled, capped credit schedule (lower exposure than our default). They want approval in writing before Procurement kickoff.

Initial thoughts:
- Risk: pilot traffic will be low but high-sensitivity; single-region for now per their note, so failure modes easier to reason about.
- Mitigation: we can accept a temporary band if we cap credits to a fixed dollar amount (e.g., equivalent to 2 weeks of forecasted pilot spend) and require a no-fault runbook (they agree to on-call communications).
- Commercial: needs a one-time discount to offset flexibility; legal needs to sign off on altered remedy language.

Marissa/Ben — can we greenlight a conditional authorization: 99.5% business-hours uptime for the 3-week pilot, credit cap at $X (to be set based on forecast), contingent on Ops guardrails and a signed addendum? If yes, I'll draft terms and loop Legal.

—Avery
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-15T15:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot - uptime target discussion

Thanks for the summary. I support a controlled, timeboxed deviation provided we hard-cap our exposure and require specific operational commitments from the customer. Proposed guardrails: 

1) Authorization: Approve a temporary business-hours uptime band of 99.5% for the three-week pilot only. No change to standard SLA outside the pilot window.
2) Credit cap: Set financial exposure cap to 2x forecasted weekly pilot spend, not to exceed $25,000.
3) Operational commitments from QuantumLytics: single-region (us-west), scheduled maintenance windows, and a documented runbook + 24/7 Slack escalation channel for the pilot.
4) Legal addendum: a one-page Rider that amends Remedies section for the pilot and expires automatically at pilot end.

If Ben concurs, Marissa approves and instructs Deal Desk to draft the addendum and return to Legal for signoff.

Marissa
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-18T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot - uptime target discussion

Marissa — I concur. Approve the pilot-specific exception under these conditions:
- Credit cap set at the lower of (2x weekly forecast) or $25,000.
- Pilot limited to 3 weeks and US-West only.
- Customer signs the one-page Rider (Legal to prepare).
- Product/Eng to enable enhanced monitoring and provide daily health reports during pilot.

Aisha — please confirm with Eliot that QuantumLytics accepts the cap and runbook requirement, and ask Legal to prepare the Rider. Once we have the signed addendum, you can proceed with onboarding.

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
